title: Storage plane — the schema every other plane is blocked on (edges, bi-temporal validity, trust tier)
description:
First of seven plane epics derived from the v2 architecture research in `project-management/design/ADVANCED_MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md`. Planning conventions, the spike protocol, and the parallel-safety rules these stories assume are in `project-management/AI_NATIVE_AGILE.md`.

**Invariant this plane owns:** writes are idempotent and linearizable per record.

The storage plane is already the SDK's most finished layer — six normalised Db2 tables, soft delete, optimistic-concurrency versioning via `version`/`StaleWriteError`, content-hash dedup, and (since migration 0008) a `MemoryOrigin` provenance enum recording which of the five internal write paths produced each row. None of that is being redone. This epic adds the three columns-and-a-table that everything in EPIC-28..33 turns out to depend on.

**A. `memory_edges` is the keystone, and its absence is why four separate features look expensive.**
Reflection (EVOL-3), cascading erasure (GOV-6), the entity graph and Personalized PageRank (EPIC-30), and Leiden community summarisation (GRPH-5) are usually costed as four independent projects. They are not: each is cheap once a typed edge table exists, and each is impossible without one. Today the only link between a derived record and its sources is `MemoryOrigin`, which records *how* a row was made but not *from what* — so a poisoned source cannot be traced to the conclusions it contaminated, and `erase_all()` deletes rows while leaving every fact consolidated out of them intact. One table (`src_id`, `dst_id`, `edge_type`, `weight`, `created_at`) with edge types `DERIVED_FROM | SUPERSEDES | CONTRADICTS | ELABORATES | CO_OCCURS` closes all four at once. It is the highest-leverage schema change in the whole v2 arc and it blocks the most work, so it is story 1.

**B. Reconciliation is temporally wrong, not merely incomplete.**
`Reconciler` + soft-supersession is the right *shape* — the SDK already distinguishes 'AI decided this was outdated' (RECONCILIATION) from 'user asked us to erase this' (`forget()`), which most systems do not. But supersession currently resolves contradictions by recency, and recency is the wrong operator. 'Lives in Berlin' (true from 2019) and 'lives in Lisbon' (true from Feb, learned in Mar) are not a contradiction — they are two facts with disjoint validity intervals, and a recency-only reconciler answers 'where did they live in 2020?' with the wrong city while reporting high confidence. The fix is the bi-temporal model standardised in SQL:2011 and used by Zep/Graphiti: keep transaction time (which the existing `created_at` / `superseded_at` pair already approximates) and add valid time (`valid_from`, `valid_to`). Defaults (`valid_from = created_at`, `valid_to = NULL`) make the migration backwards compatible and no existing behaviour changes until a caller passes an explicit interval.

**C. Trust is the one axis `MemoryOrigin` doesn't cover, and it is a security column, not a quality one.**
A memory poisoned once persists across every future session — categorically worse than prompt injection, which dies with the turn. Published rates: AgentPoison reaches >=80% attack success at <0.1% poison rate with <=1% benign degradation; MINJA reaches 98.2% injection success using *query-level access only*, i.e. without ever touching the store. The structural defence is to separate untrusted candidate memory from trusted typed memory and require mediated promotion — which is a `trust_tier` column plus a `min_trust` read parameter (GOV-1), defaulted from `MemoryOrigin` at write time. The column lands here because EPIC-32 cannot start without it; the policy that governs promotion lands there.

**Two genuine tradeoffs, both gated behind spikes rather than guessed:** edge-table growth is unbounded in principle and its real cardinality per scope is unknown (STOR-6), and storage tiering could be a status column, a separate archive table, or a distinct tablespace — with materially different erasure, backup, and index consequences (STOR-7). Neither has an obviously correct answer from reading the code.

**Scope boundary:** schema and write-path plumbing only. No retrieval behaviour changes here — `min_trust` filtering is GOV-1, as-of query paths are GRPH-6, decay-driven tier transitions are EVOL-5. The Db2 dialect seam (EPIC-25/FLEX-1) is a dependency to respect, not to redesign: every DDL statement added here goes through whatever seam FLEX-1 establishes, or documents why it can't.

**Depends on:** nothing outside itself. **Blocks:** EPIC-30 (entirely), EPIC-31 (EVOL-3, EVOL-7), EPIC-32 (GOV-1, GOV-2, GOV-6).
